extracted.intended_audience: prospective NIH grant applicants, institutional research administrators, and others new to applying for NIH funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for organizations and individuals starting the NIH extramural grants process, covering eligibility, how opportunities are announced, review/funding factors, required system registrations, and key NIH roles. Targeted at newcomers and research administrators preparing NIH grant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with NIH mission and funding categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must advance NIH's mission to seek fundamental knowledge about the nature and behavior of living systems and the application of that knowledge to enhance health, lengthen life, and reduce illness and disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH provides financial assistance for projects that advance this mission in a variety of broad research and research-related funding categories. Applicants should ensure their proposal clearly advances NIH's mission and fits within applicable funding categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding decision factors used by Institutes/Centers/Offices (ICOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: IC directors make funding decisions taking into consideration the results of the scientific peer review of the grant application, input from NIH staff, public health need, scientific opportunity, and the need to balance the scientific portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective recipients should identify ICOs that might be interested in their area of study since awards are made through ICOs; understanding these factors helps craft applications responsive to ICO priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition and success rate expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is highly competitive; NIH has three application, review, and award cycles per year and unless funds are set aside, all applications compete for the same funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall success rate is around 20% (FY2023 context). Be persistent and learn from each application; applicants who were not initially successful often secure funding on subsequent attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of set-aside funds (RFA/PAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding opportunities with set-aside funds are designated as Requests for Applications (RFA) or Program Announcements with set-aside funds (PAS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can identify them by the first three characters of their notice numbers (e.g., RFA-HL-25-123 or PAS-CA-25-123). If a FOA indicates set-aside funds, that competition may be distinct from general parent announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use correct funding opportunity type (investigator-initiated vs targeted)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH offers both investigator-initiated (unsolicited) research submitted via parent announcements or broad ICO-issued opportunities, and targeted NIH-requested funding to encourage research in specific program priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether your project is best submitted as investigator-initiated or in response to a targeted FOA; targeted FOAs may be issued to support understudied areas, program priorities, or specific infrastructure/training needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization eligibility general principle
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, organizations eligible to receive NIH grants can be domestic or foreign, public or private, non-profit or for-profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requirements vary by program and may be further restricted in individual funding opportunities; consult the Eligible Organizations section of the FOA and the NIH Grants Policy Statement: Eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign organization eligibility constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign and international organizations are eligible to apply for most NIH research project grants but are not eligible to apply for institutional training, program project, center, resource, small business, or construction grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each FOA's Foreign Organizations eligibility section states whether specific organization types are eligible. Review FOA details before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review considerations for foreign/international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications from foreign and international organizations are assessed on whether the project presents special opportunities through unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions not readily available in the U.S., and whether the project has specific relevance to the ICO mission and potential to significantly advance U.S. health sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit any unique advantages the foreign setting offers and the project's relevance to NIH/ICO missions when submitting from a foreign organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual eligibility and PD/PI designation
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant organization must designate one or more project director/principal investigators (PD/PIs) to direct the project or program supported by the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD/PIs direct the project and are accountable to the recipient organization; check the FOA for any specific individual eligibility restrictions such as citizenship requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-stage variation and citizenship considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Career stage of PD/PIs varies by program; NIH supports scientists at all stages. Generally, PD/PIs and other personnel supported by NIH research grants are not required to be U.S. citizens, though some programs have citizenship requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully read the Eligible Individuals section of the FOA for any citizenship or other individual eligibility restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Stage Investigator (ESI) definition and consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: An early stage investigator is a PI who has completed their terminal research degree or end of post-graduate clinical training within the past 10 years and who has not previously competed successfully as a PD/PI for a substantial NIH independent research award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers give ESIs special consideration and meritorious ESI applications may be prioritized for funding; NIH has programs targeted for ESIs (e.g., Stephen I. Katz ESI Research Project Grant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand NIH staff roles (Program Official, Scientific Review Officer, Grants Management Officer/Specialist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Official (PO): responsible for programmatic, scientific, and/or technical aspects; Scientific Review Officer (SRO): manages peer review and conflicts of interest; Grants Management Officer/Specialist (GMO/GMS): handles business management aspects including administrative compliance, award negotiation, and policy interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing who does what helps applicants know whom to contact at different stages and how programmatic vs administrative concerns are handled; see 'Understand Staff Roles' for contact tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: System for Award Management (SAM) and UEI registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All organizations must register in SAM and establish a unique entity identifier (UEI) prior to doing business with the U.S. federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same UEI across all organization registrations; SAM is also the place to search for federal contract opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov role and submission routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov is the central portal used by federal grant-making agencies and their applicants to find and apply for funding; it receives application submissions on behalf of NIH and forwards them for processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Grants.gov to Explore NIH Grant Opportunities and to submit applications when required; NIH-specific filters are available to identify FOAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The eRA Commons allows applicants, recipients, and federal staff to securely share, manage, and process grant-related information, track submission status, application assignment and review info, award info, and supports post-award reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators and institutional officials use eRA Commons to check assembled application images, summary statements, scores, notices of award, and for post-submission administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASSIST as an application submission option
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST (Application Submission System & Interface for Submission Tracking) is one of several submission options available to prepare and submit grant applications electronically to NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with ASSIST if you plan to use it to assemble and submit applications; other submission pathways also exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons Signing Official (SO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing Official holds authority to legally bind the institution, assume responsibility for adhering to federal grant administration requirements, register and maintain institutional profile data, access info for all applications and grants, and create/administer user accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure an authorized SO is designated during organization registration and that they maintain accurate institutional data in eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons Project Director/Principal Investigator (PD/PI) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PI holds the eRA Commons PI role, directs the project, is accountable to the recipient organization for conduct of the project, performs/delegates tasks such as maintaining profile info, checking application status and assembled application image, and accesses summary statements, scores, and notices of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the PD/PI has an eRA Commons account with the correct role and regularly monitors application materials and review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization registration process and authorized registrant requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple organization registrations are required (eRA Commons, SAM, Grants.gov, SBA if applicable) and the person who registers the organization must be authorized to act for the organization and assume obligations imposed by federal laws and award conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This registrant (entity administrator, SO, or AOR) is responsible for initial registration, maintaining organization information, and authorizing other individuals to perform related functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards are typically made to organizations (not individuals)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH typically makes awards to organizations, not individuals; in rare cases an unaffiliated individual may need to register as an organization (e.g., Loan Repayment Program contracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Special Registration Instructions for Unaffiliated/Independent Applicants for guidance on how individuals without institutional affiliation should register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating system accounts for investigators and individual users
rubrics_metrics.description: Once organizational registrations are complete, individuals responsible for maintaining organization information can assist in creating individual user accounts and affiliating principal investigator accounts (PI role) in eRA Commons, Grants.gov, SAM, and Login.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow system-specific instructions for creating accounts and assigning roles; consult Accounts Module Online Help for eRA Commons.
